newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho court reinstates premier to ruling party.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho court reinstates premier to ruling party.

text.p: Lesotho's High Court on Friday ordered the reinstatement of besieged Premier Ntsu Mokhehle as leader of the ruling Basotholand Congress Party, South African state radio reported.
Mokhehle was ousted as leader of the BCP last month at a conference called by a rival faction within the party after accusations the tiny kingdom was drifting into lawlessness.
Judge Winston Makwetu ruled in Maseru that the conference which resolved Mokhehle should be "relieved of his leadership" was unconstitutional, effectively reinstating him.
BCP deputy leader Matlejane Qhobela heads the rival faction within the ruling party which has been lobbying for a leadership change ahead of a general election scheduled for next year.
Despite the internal party wrangling and his poor health, diplomats told Reuters that Mokhehle, 78, had retained strong support from voters and party members and was not necessarily a spent force.

Mokhehle has weathered a series of crises since March 1993 when he won the first democratic polls in two decades. The most recent was in February when Lesotho army troops were called in to end an 11-day police mutiny.
